jobDescription: We are a digital bank offering current accounts and small-business lending. The Financial Crime Investigations Team Leader supervises six investigators who review transaction-monitoring alerts escalated by the first-line team, quality-checks investigation decisions, drafts suspicious activity reports for the nominated officer's approval and trains new investigators. The role needs the CAMS certification and at least five years of anti-money-laundering investigation work, and the team leader reports to the head of financial crime operations and joins the monthly meeting with the nominated officer on open cases.
requirements: Supervises a team of investigators reviewing escalated transaction-monitoring alerts.
Holds the Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist (CAMS) certification.
Has at least five years of anti-money-laundering investigation experience.
Quality-checks investigation decisions and drafts suspicious activity reports for the nominated officer.
Designs and delivers training for new investigators.

evidence.text: Investigations Team Leader, Tamworth & Lyle Bank (June 2023 to September 2026): supervised the alert queue of a five-person investigation pod, allocating escalated alerts each morning and reviewing every closure decision before it was filed.
Drafted suspicious activity reports for the nominated officer's approval and kept the quality-check log recording the reviewer, the outcome and any rework for each case.
Investigator, Calder Building Society (April 2019 to May 2023): investigated alerts on personal accounts, including mule-account patterns and third-party cash deposits.
CAMS (Certified Anti-Money Laundering Specialist), awarded by ACAMS in November 2021, member ID 7740215.
Delivered the two-day induction on alert investigation to the investigators who joined in 2025, using the materials prepared by the compliance training team.
Work sample: an anonymised quality-check log for one month, showing 42 closed investigations, the reviewer for each, the outcome category and the three cases returned for rework with the reasons.

HR verification note: the Investigator role at Calder Building Society and the Investigations Team Leader role at Tamworth & Lyle Bank were checked against references from both employers; together they cover seven years and six months in all of anti-money-laundering investigation work.
Recruiter verification: ACAMS member ID 7740215 was checked on the ACAMS certification directory and the CAMS credential is shown as active.

propositions.text: The candidate holds an active CAMS certification, awarded in November 2021 and checked on the ACAMS certification directory.
propositions.rationale: The resume lists the certification and member ID and the recruiter verification records the directory check.

propositions.text: The candidate has seven years and six months of anti-money-laundering investigation experience, confirmed by employer references.
propositions.rationale: The resume gives the dated roles and the HR verification note states the employer-checked total.

propositions.text: The candidate supervised a five-person investigation pod, allocating escalated alerts daily and reviewing every closure decision before filing.
propositions.rationale: The resume describes the supervision and the work sample shows the monthly quality-check log.

gold.expectedGap: Designing training is not documented; the candidate delivered an induction using materials prepared by the compliance training team.
gold.expectedBoundaryNote: Keep the verified CAMS credential, the employer-confirmed total of seven years and six months and the documented supervision and quality-check work; do not describe the candidate as having designed the induction.
followUpTargets: Ask whether the candidate has designed or changed any training material for investigators and how its effect was checked.
